page: OVHcloud l40s-90 is a cloud GPU instance built for graphics computing and artificial intelligence workloads. It is powered by a dedicated 15-core AMD EPYC 9124 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.75 GHz, with one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity is set to 90.0 GB of system RAM, providing 6.0 GB per physical core. For primary acceleration, the instance includes a dedicated NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU with 48 GB of VRAM. Bundled local storage includes a 400 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Hardware benchmark scores demonstrate distinct compute tiers between CPU execution and GPU acceleration. In single-core testing, the AMD processor yields top-quartile results, including a 1941.0 Geekbench single-core score and a 3043.17 stress-ng rating. Multi-threaded CPU metrics settle into average percentiles, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 11588.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 34459.04. Conversely, the bundled NVIDIA L40S accelerator demonstrates top-decile performance across large language model benchmarks. In prompt processing, it processes 13644.94 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models and 6030.41 tokens/sec on 7B models. Generation tasks deliver 136.71 tokens/sec on 7B models and 15.72 tokens/sec on 70B models.

The architecture balances high-end GPU throughput with an asymmetric 15-core CPU configuration. Memory bandwidth for un-cached large block reads reaches 49.41 GB/sec, supporting standard ingestion pipelines. The 400 GB NVMe drive offers high local IOPS for fast model caching and scratch space, though its capacity restricts massive local dataset storage without external volumes. Because public IPv4 connectivity requires manual allocation due to zero complimentary addresses, networking is primarily optimized for intra-datacenter fabrics up to its 8 Gbps threshold.

The OVHcloud l40s-90 delivers specialized cost efficiency for deep learning inference, model fine-tuning, 3D graphics rendering, and batch video processing. The 48 GB VRAM pool makes it particularly suitable for serving medium-to-large foundation models without requiring expensive multi-GPU arrays.

Primary computational throughput is driven by an NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S accelerator with 48 GB of VRAM, supported by a 400 GB local NVMe SSD and 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU execution alongside average multi-core results, while GPU evaluation shows top-tier performance across large language model inference suites. With 6.0 GB of RAM per core and a massive VRAM buffer, this configuration is well tailored for LLM serving, generative AI pipelines, graphics rendering, and computer vision tasks requiring high GPU compute density.
